subject: spanish
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.explain: “La feria” means “a fair/funfair”, such as the famous Feria de Sevilla.
'Descargar' means 'to download', so 'descargar música' = 'to download music'.

questions.q: How do you say “I like reading novels”?
questions.explain: “Leer novelas” = to read novels, so “Me gusta leer novelas”.
'La Nochebuena' (24 December) means 'Christmas Eve'; 'la Nochevieja' is New Year's Eve.
“Las legumbres” are “pulses/legumes” such as beans, lentils and chickpeas.

questions.q: How do you say “It is a tradition that lasts three days”?
options: Es una tradición que duran tres días
Es una tradición que dura tres años
Era una tradición que dura tres días
Es una tradición que dura tres días
questions.explain: “Durar” = to last, so “que dura tres días” = “that lasts three days”.
'El tabaquismo' is the habit/addiction of smoking, not a shop (that would be 'el estanco').

questions.q: What does “una película de dibujos animados” mean?
questions.explain: “Dibujos animados” means “cartoons”, so it is “an animated/cartoon film”.
“Los pulmones” means “the lungs”.

questions.q: How do you say “We light candles and sing songs”?
questions.explain: “Encender velas” = to light candles and “cantar canciones” = to sing songs.

questions.q: How would you write 'trabajador' to describe a hard-working woman?
questions.explain: Adjectives ending in -dor add -a for the feminine singular, so a hard-working woman is 'trabajadora'.

questions.q: What does 'llevar una vida sana' mean?
questions.explain: 'Sano/a' means 'healthy', so 'llevar una vida sana' = 'to lead a healthy life'.
'La asignatura' is a false friend: it means 'school subject', not 'signature' (which is 'la firma').

questions.q: How do you say 'I do exercise to keep fit'?
options: Hago ejercicio porque estoy en forma
Hace ejercicio para mantenerme en forma
Hago ejercicio para mantenerme en forma
questions.explain: 'Mantenerse en forma' = 'to keep fit' and 'para' = 'in order to'; 'hago' is the correct first-person form.

questions.q: How do you say 'We celebrate my grandmother's birthday'?
options: Celebramos el cumpleaños de mi abuela
Celebro el cumpleaños de mi abuela
Celebramos la Navidad de mi abuela
Celebramos el cumpleaños de mi abuelo
questions.explain: 'Celebramos' = 'we celebrate' and 'de mi abuela' = 'my grandmother's', so the first option is correct.
“El villancico” means “a Christmas carol”.

questions.q: Which sentence means “I'm trying to eat less sugar”?
questions.explain: “Intento comer menos azúcar” = “I'm trying to eat less sugar”.

questions.q: What does “una entrada” mean (for a concert)?
questions.explain: “Una entrada” means a “ticket” for an event (it can also mean a starter or doorway).
'Embarazada' is a classic false friend: it means 'pregnant', not 'embarrassed' (which is 'avergonzado/a').
“La madrastra” means “stepmother”; “madrina” is godmother and “suegra” is mother-in-law.
“Los sellos” here means “stamps”, so “coleccionar sellos” = “to collect stamps”.
“El ajedrez” means “chess”; “el ajo” (garlic) is a near-miss distractor.
